title: Maximize the Confusion of an Exam
statement:
The string `answerKey` lists the answers of a true/false exam in order: `answerKey[i]` is `'T'` or `'F'` for question `i`. You may flip at most `k` of these answers, turning any chosen `'T'` into `'F'` or any chosen `'F'` into `'T'`.

After your changes, look at the longest block of consecutive questions that all have the same answer (all `'T'` or all `'F'`). Return the greatest length such a block can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

A block of questions can be made all the same exactly when its rarer answer appears at most `k` times: flip those and the block is uniform. Checking every block is O(n²). Since growing a block can only make its rarer count bigger, a sliding window works: extend the right end one question at a time, and shrink from the left only while the window holds more than `k` of both answers.

## Approach

1. Keep a `count` map from `'T'` and `'F'` to how often each appears in the window `answerKey[left..right]`; both counts start at `0`, as do `left` and `best`.
2. For each `right`, raise the count of `answerKey[right]` by one.
3. While `Math.min(count.get('T'), count.get('F')) > k`, lower the count of `answerKey[left]` by one and move `left` forward.
4. The window is now fixable; update `best` with its length `right - left + 1`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`answerKey = "TTFF"`, `k = 2`. At `right = 0` and `1`, the window is `"T"` then `"TT"` with no `'F'`, so `best = 2`. At `right = 2`, the window `"TTF"` has `min(2, 1) = 1 <= 2`, so `best = 3`. At `right = 3`, `"TTFF"` has `min(2, 2) = 2 <= 2`, so `best = 4`. The window never shrinks, and the answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `right` and `left` each move across the string at most once.
- Space: O(1): the map only ever holds two counters.

## Pitfalls

- You may flip toward either answer; running the window only for "make everything `'T'`" misses blocks that should become `'F'` (Example 2).
- Measure the window after shrinking it, not before, or an invalid window can be counted.
- The flips are at most `k`, not exactly `k`, so an all-equal string returns its full length.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | map from `'T'` and `'F'` to how many of each the window holds |
| `left`, `right` | the window's first and last question |
| `best` | the longest fixable window seen so far |

narration.2: A map counts how many 'T' and 'F' answers the current window holds; both start at zero.
narration.3: The window starts at the first question.
narration.4: No window has been measured yet.
narration.5: Grow the window by one question at a time on the right.
narration.6: Add the new question's answer to its count in the map.
narration.7: If both answers appear more than k times, flipping the rarer one would need too many changes.
narration.8: Drop the leftmost question's answer from the counts...
narration.9: ...and move the window's left edge forward.
narration.11: The window can now be made uniform, so compare its length with the best.
narration.13: Return the longest window that k flips can make uniform.
